lessons.title: 副词的定义与本质
lessons.meta: 给动作、性质或整句增加背景与范围
examples: Probably, the train will arrive soon.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: calmly 不改变“回答”这件事，而是补充回答以什么方式发生。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: very 不直接说明 water，而是把形容词 cold 的程度提高。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Probably 不是修饰某一个词，而是表示说话人对整件事发生可能性的判断。

rules: 副词的本质是给动作、性质、另一个副词或整句话增加时间、地点、方式、程度、频率、态度或范围。
判断副词不能只看 -ly；关键是看它在修饰谁、增加什么信息。
副词的位置常提示作用范围：离哪个成分更近，通常更直接限定哪个成分。

questions.question: calmly 在“Mia answered calmly.”中补充什么？
questions.correct: calmly 说明回答的方式。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：calmly 说明回答的方式。

questions.question: very 在“very cold”中修饰什么？
questions.correct: very 直接限定 cold 的程度。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：very 直接限定 cold 的程度。

questions.question: Probably 在句首通常限定什么？
questions.correct: Probably 表示对整件事可能性的判断。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Probably 表示对整件事可能性的判断。

narration.text:
只说“米娅回答了”，事情已经完整；如果加上“平静地”，我们就知道她是怎么回答的。这个后来补上的词，不负责说人或东西“什么样”，而是在给动作加细节。这样的词常常叫副词。副词还能给一个性质加程度，甚至表达说话人对整件事的态度。<#0.8#>
先听。<#0.4#>Mia answered calmly。<#0.8#>主干只是 Mia answered。calmly 回答“怎么回答”，给动作 answered 加上方式。在句子里，这份补充方式的工作叫状语。<#0.8#>
再听。<#0.4#>The water is very cold。<#0.8#>very 不是在说明 water，也不是在说明 is，它只把 cold 的程度往上推，变成“非常冷”。所以副词不只跟动作，也可以跟形容词。<#0.8#>
再听一句。<#0.4#>Probably, the train will arrive soon。<#0.8#>soon 只告诉我们什么时候到；Probably 管的是整件事，表示说话人觉得“可能会到”。两个词都属于副词，管的范围却不一样。去掉 Probably，火车到达这件事还在，只是说话人的把握没有说出来。<#0.7#>
判断时别看到 ly 就直接下结论，因为 friendly 不是这里说的副词，fast 也没有 ly。先问这个词在给哪个动作、哪种性质或哪件事加信息；再问加的是时间、方式、程度还是态度；最后用整句意思检查它到底管到哪里。

lessons.title: 副词在句中做什么
lessons.meta: 修饰动词、形容词、副词或全句
examples: He finished the task remarkably quickly.

analyses.label: 程度副词：修饰副词 quickly
方式副词：修饰动词 finished

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: politely 直接修饰 answered，说明回答采用什么方式。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: very 修饰形容词 cold，只改变寒冷的程度。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately 评价“所有人安全到达”整件事；safely 则说明 arrived 的方式。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: remarkably 修饰 quickly，quickly 再修饰 finished，形成两层修饰关系。

rules: 副词可以修饰动词，说明动作的方式等信息。
程度副词可以修饰形容词。
程度副词也可以修饰另一个副词。
句子副词可以评价或限定整个句子。

questions.question: She spoke ___.
questions.correct: clearly 修饰动词 spoke，作方式状语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：clearly 修饰动词 spoke，作方式状语。

questions.question: The test is ___ easy.
questions.correct: quite 是程度副词，修饰 easy。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：quite 是程度副词，修饰 easy。

questions.question: ___, nobody was hurt.
questions.correct: Luckily 评价整个句子。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Luckily 评价整个句子。

questions.question: She completed the work extremely ___.
questions.correct: extremely 修饰副词 carefully；carefully 再修饰 completed。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：extremely 修饰副词 carefully；carefully 再修饰 completed。

narration.text:
同样是副词，作用目标可能完全不同。先听：<#0.4#>Mia answered politely。<#0.8#>主干 Mia answered 已经说明她回答了，politely 只补充“怎样回答”，直接修饰动词 answered。
再听：<#0.4#>The water is very cold。<#0.8#>very 不说明 water，也不说明 is，它只把 cold 的程度提高，所以修饰形容词。<#0.7#>
Fortunately, everyone arrived safely 里有两个副词。safely 只说明 arrived 的方式；Fortunately 表示说话人觉得“幸好大家安全到达”，评价的是整件事。把 Fortunately 去掉，事件仍在，只是说话人的态度没了。He finished the task remarkably quickly 中，quickly 说明完成得怎样，remarkably 再加强 quickly，形成“非常快地”。一个副词也能修饰另一个副词。
判断副词的工作，先别只找 ly。给副词画一根箭头：指向动作，就是修饰动词；指向性质词，就是修饰形容词；指向另一个方式或程度词，就是修饰副词；若它在评价整句话的可能性、幸运与否或说话态度，就按句子副词处理。

lessons.title: 副词与状语有什么区别
examples: She spoke in a soft voice.
She spoke when the room became quiet.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: softly 既是副词这一词类，在句中又承担方式状语这一功能。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: in a soft voice 整体是状语，但它是介词短语，不是一个副词。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: when 从句说明说话时间，整体作状语；不能把整条从句叫作副词。

rules: 副词是词类；状语是句子成分，二者不能画等号。
副词可以作状语，但介词短语、名词短语和非谓语短语也能作状语。
从句也能作状语，表示时间、原因、条件、让步等关系。

questions.question: softly 是什么词类？
questions.correct: softly 是副词，在句中可作状语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：softly 是副词，在句中可作状语。

questions.question: in the morning 是副词吗？

options.text: No; it is a prepositional phrase.
Yes; every adverbial is an adverb.

questions.correct: 它能作状语，但形式是介词短语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：它能作状语，但形式是介词短语。

questions.question: when he arrived 整体是什么？
questions.correct: 它是从句，整体承担状语功能。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：它是从句，整体承担状语功能。

narration.text:
老师问“softly 是副词还是状语”，答案可能是：两个说法都对，但回答的不是同一个问题。<#0.4#>She spoke softly。<#0.8#>softly 这个单词属于副词；它在句中回答“怎样说话”，承担的工作叫方式状语。副词是词的类别，状语是句子里的职位。
这个职位不只给副词坐。<#0.4#>She spoke in a soft voice。<#0.8#>in a soft voice 是介词短语，不是一个副词，但整块仍回答“怎样说话”，所以也作方式状语。<#0.7#>
She spoke when the room became quiet 中，when the room became quiet 里面有自己的主语和谓语，是一个从句；它整体回答“什么时候说话”，作时间状语。名词短语、非谓语短语也可能承担状语工作。
区分时分两层检查：先看形式，一个词是什么词类，一组词是介词短语、名词短语还是从句；再看功能，它对主句补充时间、地点、方式、原因还是条件。看到副词可以判断它常作状语，但看到状语绝不能反推它一定是副词。

lessons.title: 副词有哪些类别
lessons.meta: 时间、地点、方式、频率、程度

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: 英语常把地点放在时间前；中文更常说“明天在外面见”。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: often 说明频率，quietly 说明方式，here 说明地点；三个副词各回答不同问题。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: too 说明 heavy 的程度已经超过合适范围。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately 评价整件事，soon 则说明 stopped 发生的时间。

rules: 时间副词说明动作发生的时间。
地点副词说明动作发生的地点或方向。
方式副词说明动作怎样发生。
频率副词说明动作发生得多频繁。
程度副词说明性质、状态或动作的程度。
评注性副词表达说话者对全句的态度或判断。

questions.question: We met ___ yesterday.
questions.correct: there 是地点副词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：there 是地点副词。

questions.question: He ___ walks to school.
questions.correct: usually 是频率副词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：usually 是频率副词。

questions.question: The box is ___ small.
questions.correct: quite 是程度副词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：quite 是程度副词。

questions.question: We will leave ___.
questions.correct: tomorrow 是时间副词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：tomorrow 是时间副词。

questions.question: She answered ___.
questions.correct: politely 是方式副词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：politely 是方式副词。

questions.question: ___, the key was still there.
questions.correct: Luckily 是评价全句的评注性副词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Luckily 是评价全句的评注性副词。

narration.text:
一句话里可能同时塞进好几种背景。<#0.4#>We will meet outside tomorrow。<#0.8#>outside 回答“在哪里见”，是地点副词；tomorrow 回答“什么时候见”，是时间副词。分类不是看它们站在句尾，而是看各自补了什么信息。
再听：<#0.4#>She often reads quietly here。<#0.8#>often 说明阅读发生得多频繁，是频率副词；quietly 回答“怎样读”，是方式副词；here 指出地点。三个词都和 reads 有关，却各自回答不同问题。<#0.7#>
The bag is too heavy 中，too 不说明时间地点，而是把 heavy 推到“过于重”的程度，叫程度副词。Fortunately, the rain stopped soon 里，soon 给 stopped 加时间；Fortunately 则评价“雨停了”整件事，表达说话人的态度。
分类时先找副词的作用对象，再逐个提问：何时是时间，何地是地点，怎样是方式，多常是频率，到什么程度是程度；若它表达对整件事的幸运、意外或把握，就归入评注性句子副词。一个句子可以同时出现多类，不必只选一个。

lessons.title: 副词怎样构成
lessons.meta: -ly 拼写、同形副词与意义变化

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 大多数方式副词在形容词后加 -ly：quick 变 quickly。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 辅音字母加 y 结尾时，通常把 y 变 i 再加 -ly。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: true 变 truly 时去掉 e；whole 变 wholly 也需单独注意。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: fast 不加 -ly 也能作副词；不是所有副词都以 -ly 结尾。

rules: 许多方式副词由形容词加 -ly 构成。
辅音字母 + y 常变 y 为 i 再加 -ly。
部分词有特殊拼写，如 true–truly、whole–wholly、full–fully。
fast、hard、late、early 等可直接作副词；加 -ly 后有时意义会改变。

questions.question: careful 的副词是？
questions.correct: careful 加 -ly 形成 carefully。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：careful 加 -ly 形成 carefully。

questions.question: happy 的副词是？
questions.correct: y 变 i 再加 -ly。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：y 变 i 再加 -ly。

questions.question: true 的副词是？
questions.correct: true 去 e 变 truly。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：true 去 e 变 truly。

questions.question: He works ___.
questions.correct: hard 表示“努力地”；hardly 表示“几乎不”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：hard 表示“努力地”；hardly 表示“几乎不”。

narration.text:
想把 quick 变成“快速地”，最常见的办法是加 ly：<#0.4#>quick → quickly。<#0.8#>但不能只在每个形容词后面随手粘 ly，拼写和词义都要检查。
第二组是 happy → happily。happy 结尾是辅音字母加 y，变副词时先把 y 改成 i，再加 ly。<#0.7#>第三组 true → truly，要去掉结尾的 e，再加 ly。这些变化说明构词还要处理原词拼写。<#0.7#>
最后看 He runs fast。fast 没有 ly，却直接修饰 runs，说明动作怎样发生。不是所有副词都以 ly 结尾，也不是所有形容词都必须加 ly 才能承担副词功能。
构词时先确认句中真的需要副词；普通方式词可尝试加 ly；遇到辅音加 y、true、full 等词先处理拼写；最后检查这个词是否本来就能同形作副词，以及 ly 形式有没有产生新意思。不能用“有 ly 就是副词、没 ly 就不是”来判断。

lessons.title: 副词放在哪里
examples: Yesterday, we finished the work quickly.

analyses.label: 频率状语：置于实义动词前
频率状语：置于 be 后
频率状语：置于第一个助动词后

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: usually 放在实义动词 walks 前，表示走路上学的通常频率。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: be 动词 is 在前，频率副词 always 放在 is 后、表语 kind 前。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Yesterday 前置建立时间背景；quickly 放句尾说明完成工作的方式。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: never 放在第一个助动词 has 后、主要动词 visited 前。

rules: 频率副词通常放在实义动词前。
频率副词通常放在 be 动词后。
有助动词时，频率副词通常放在第一个助动词后。
方式副词常放在动词及其宾语之后。
时间副词可放句首或句尾；放在句首时常用逗号隔开。

questions.question: Tom ___ gets up early.
questions.correct: often 通常放在实义动词 gets 前。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：often 通常放在实义动词 gets 前。

questions.question: She is ___ late.
questions.correct: 频率副词置于 be 动词之后。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：频率副词置于 be 动词之后。

questions.question: He completed the task ___.
questions.correct: 方式副词 carefully 常放在宾语之后。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：方式副词 carefully 常放在宾语之后。

questions.question: She has ___ seen snow.
questions.correct: never 放在第一个助动词 has 后。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：never 放在第一个助动词 has 后。

questions.question: Choose the natural time-adverb position.
questions.correct: 时间副词可置于句首，并用逗号隔开。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：时间副词可置于句首，并用逗号隔开。

narration.text:
你想说 Lily 通常走路上学，usually 放哪儿？英语说：<#0.4#>Lily usually walks to school。<#0.8#>walks 是实义动词，频率副词通常站在它前面。
换成 be，位置就换了：<#0.4#>Lily is always kind。<#0.8#>always 放在 is 后。第三句 Yesterday, we finished the work quickly 把时间提到句首作背景，让方式副词 quickly 放在动词和宾语之后。<#0.7#>
最后看 She has never visited London。句中有助动词 has，never 放在第一个助动词后、主要动词 visited 前。可以把频率副词想成靠近谓语核心的中间位置，但具体落点要看前面是 be 还是助动词。
操作时先给副词分类。频率词遇到实义动词放前，遇到 be 放后，有助动词放第一个助动词后；方式词通常放动词和宾语之后；时间词可放句首或句尾，句首背景后常加逗号。最后再按想强调的信息作小幅调整。

lessons.title: 形容词还是副词
lessons.meta: 系动词、行为动词与同形词
examples: The child smelled the flower carefully.

analyses.label: 以 -ly 结尾的形容词作表语

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: smell 是系动词，sweet 说明 flowers 的性质，所以用形容词。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: smelled 表示闻的动作，carefully 说明动作方式，所以用副词。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: fast 形式不变，但在这里修饰 moves，因此是副词。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: friendly 虽以 -ly 结尾，却说明 neighbour 的性质，是形容词表语。

rules: 系动词后用形容词说明主语。
行为动词通常由副词修饰。
fast、hard、late、early 等可直接作副词，不加 -ly。
friendly、lovely 等虽然以 -ly 结尾，却通常是形容词。

questions.question: The music sounds ___.
questions.correct: sound 作系动词，后用形容词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：sound 作系动词，后用形容词。

questions.question: She sings ___.
questions.correct: 副词 beautifully 修饰行为动词 sings。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：副词 beautifully 修饰行为动词 sings。

questions.question: He works ___.
questions.correct: hard 可直接作副词，表示“努力地”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：hard 可直接作副词，表示“努力地”。

questions.question: She gave me a ___ smile.
questions.correct: friendly 是形容词，修饰名词 smile。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：friendly 是形容词，修饰名词 smile。

narration.text:
闻到花香时，英语说：<#0.4#>The flowers smell sweet。<#0.8#>这里 smell 是“闻起来”，像一座桥把 flowers 和 sweet 连起来。sweet 说明花本身的性质，所以在这里是形容词。
如果孩子主动去闻花，句子变成：<#0.4#>The child smelled the flower carefully。<#0.8#>smelled 现在是行为动作，carefully 回答孩子“怎样闻”，所以用副词。判断形式前，要先分清动词是在连接主语状态，还是在表示真实动作。<#0.7#>
词尾也会骗人。The train moves fast 里，fast 没有 ly，却直接说明 moves 的方式。Our new neighbour is friendly 中，friendly 虽然以 ly 结尾，却通过 is 说明 neighbour，所以是形容词。
选择时先问被说明的是人或物的状态，还是动作发生的方式。系动词后说明主语，用形容词；行为动词旁说明动作，通常用副词。接着检查例句中的 fast 和 friendly 这类形式，不能只靠 ly 词尾下结论。

lessons.title: 副词也能比较吗
lessons.meta: 比较级、最高级与同级比较
examples: Ben answered more carefully than I did.
Of all the runners, Leo ran the fastest.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: faster 比较 Amy 和 Sue 跑步的速度，修饰 runs。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: carefully 是 -ly 副词，比较级在前面加 more。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: of all the runners 给出三者以上范围，因此用副词最高级 the fastest。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: better 是 well 的不规则比较级，说明表现比以前更好。

rules: 短副词常加 -er/-est 构成比较级和最高级。
多数 -ly 副词用 more/most 构成比较级和最高级。
well–better–best、badly–worse–worst 等是不规则变化。

questions.question: Jane speaks ___ than before.
questions.correct: -ly 副词通常用 more 构成比较级。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：-ly 副词通常用 more 构成比较级。

questions.question: Tom runs ___ of the three.
questions.correct: 三者范围使用副词最高级。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：三者范围使用副词最高级。

questions.question: She did ___ than yesterday.
questions.correct: well 的比较级是不规则形式 better。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：well 的比较级是不规则形式 better。

narration.text:
比赛时不只比较谁更高，还会比较谁跑得更快。<#0.4#>Amy runs faster than Sue。<#0.8#>faster 说明动作 runs 的速度更高。fast 是短副词，比较级直接加 er，最高级加 est。
若副词以 ly 结尾，通常不把词拉得更长。<#0.4#>Ben answered more carefully than I did。<#0.8#>carefully 前加 more 表示更仔细；三者以上可用 most carefully。Of all the runners, Leo ran the fastest 画出多人范围，用 fastest 选出速度最高者。<#0.7#>
还有不规则形式。Nora performed better than before 中，better 是 well 的比较级；well、better、best 要整体记。badly 则变 worse、worst。
操作时先确认比较的是动作方式或程度，而不是人或物的性质；再看副词形式。短副词常加 er 或 est，多数 ly 副词用 more 或 most；最后检查 well、badly 等不规则变化，并用 than 或范围短语说清比较基准。

lessons.title: 程度副词怎样搭配
examples: The room is warm enough for the baby.
The box is too heavy for me to lift.
It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it.
The question was so difficult that nobody answered it.

analyses.label: 动作执行者与结果结构

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: enough 放在 warm 后，表示温暖程度达到婴儿所需标准。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: too 放在 heavy 前，表示重量超过“我能抬起”的限度。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: such 修饰整个名词短语 a difficult question，that 从句说明结果。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: so 直接修饰形容词 difficult，that 从句说明困难造成的结果。

rules: enough 修饰形容词或副词时放在其后。
too 放在形容词或副词前，常表示“过于……而不能……”。
so 修饰形容词或副词，如 so difficult。
such 修饰名词短语，如 such a difficult task。

questions.question: She is old ___ to travel alone.
questions.correct: enough 修饰形容词时放在其后。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：enough 修饰形容词时放在其后。

questions.question: The water is ___ hot to drink.
questions.correct: too...to 表示过热而不能喝。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：too...to 表示过热而不能喝。

questions.question: It was ___ an exciting match.
questions.correct: an exciting match 是名词短语，前用 such。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：an exciting match 是名词短语，前用 such。

questions.question: The film was ___ exciting that we watched it twice.
questions.correct: exciting 是形容词，前用 so。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：exciting 是形容词，前用 so。

narration.text:
同样是“很暖”，几个程度词站的位置不一样。宝宝待在房间里刚好合适，可以说：<#0.4#>The room is warm enough for the baby。<#0.8#>enough 放在形容词 warm 后，表示程度已经足够。
箱子重到我抬不动，就说：<#0.4#>The box is too heavy for me to lift。<#0.8#>too 放在 heavy 前，表示程度超过合适范围，后面的 for me to lift 说明对谁、做什么来说太重。<#0.7#>
第三句 It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it 中，such 抓住整个名词短语 a difficult question。第四句 The question was so difficult that nobody answered it 里，so 直接修饰形容词 difficult。两句结果相同，程度词后面的结构不同。
选择时先看程度词后面的中心。修饰形容词或副词，enough 放后面，too 和 so 放前面；修饰带冠词和名词的整块，用 such。若后面还有 that 从句，再判断前面突出的是性质程度，还是包含冠词、形容词和名词的完整名词短语。

lessons.title: 副词修饰范围会改变意思
lessons.meta: only · even · almost · 句子副词
examples: Even Ben almost missed the bus.

analyses.label: 聚焦副词：强调出乎意料

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: Only Mia 表示“只有米娅（别人没有）”，only 的位置决定被限定的信息。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: only solved 强调“只解出了”，没有做更多事情；与 Only Mia 的焦点不同。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Even 聚焦 Ben，强调他能理解出乎意料；almost 修饰 missed，表示差点错过但实际没有。

rules: only 应尽量靠近被限定成分，位置变化可能改变句意。
even 强调出乎意料的焦点。
almost 表示某事接近发生但实际没有发生。

questions.question: 哪一句表示“只有李华通过了考试”？

options.text: Only Li Hua passed the exam.
Li Hua only passed the exam.

questions.correct: only 紧靠 Li Hua，限定“谁”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：only 紧靠 Li Hua，限定“谁”。

questions.question: She ___ missed the bus; she arrived just in time.
questions.correct: almost missed 表示“差点错过但没有”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：almost missed 表示“差点错过但没有”。

questions.question: ___ Ben understood the difficult puzzle.
questions.correct: Even 聚焦 Ben，强调结果出乎预料。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Even 聚焦 Ben，强调结果出乎预料。

narration.text:
一句话只挪动 only，重点就可能换人。<#0.4#>Only Mia solved the puzzle。<#0.8#>only 靠近 Mia，排除的是其他人：只有米娅解开了。第二句 Mia only solved the puzzle 中，only 靠近 solved，更容易表示她只是解开了，没有做别的。副词影响哪一块内容，叫作用范围；位置常在帮我们标范围。<#0.7#>
最后看 Even Ben almost missed the bus。even 把 Ben 标成出乎意料的人，暗示连他都差点误车；almost 修饰 missed，表示事情接近发生，但最后没有真的错过。两个副词在同一句里，各有自己的焦点。<#0.7#>
判断时给 only、even、almost 各画一条括号，圈住它最直接限定的成分；再用排除、意外或接近发生来改述意思。若一句话可能圈出两种范围，就把副词挪到目标成分旁边，或改写句子，让焦点唯一。

lessons.title: 易混副词
examples: I have hardly seen her lately.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: hard 修饰 works，表示“努力地”，与 hardly“几乎不”不是程度变化。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: hardly 表示几乎没见过；lately 表示最近，不能分别理解成 hard 和 late 的普通 -ly 形式。

rules: hard 是“努力地/猛烈地”，hardly 是“几乎不”。
late 是“迟”，lately 是“最近”。

questions.question: She studies ___.
questions.correct: hard 表示“努力地”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：hard 表示“努力地”。

questions.question: Have you seen Tom ___?
questions.correct: lately 表示“最近”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：lately 表示“最近”。

narration.text:
有些副词只差两个字母，意思却拐到另一条路。<#0.4#>He works hard every day。<#0.8#>hard 修饰 works，表示“努力地”。如果换成 hardly，句子就变成“他几乎不工作”，不是“更努力”。
再听：<#0.4#>I have hardly seen her lately。<#0.8#>hardly 表示“几乎没见过”，lately 表示“最近”。这里两个 ly 形式都不能从 hard 和 late 的表面意思直接推出来。<#0.7#>
第二句同时放入 hardly 和 lately，正好展示 ly 形式可能形成独立词义。lately 只谈最近一段时间，不能按 late 的“迟”直接推导。类似词必须把整组意义分开存，而不是把 ly 当作普通构词尾。
遇到 hard 或 hardly，先问句子要表达努力，还是几乎不；遇到 late 或 lately，先问是某次到得迟，还是最近这段时间。选完后把中文意思完整代回原句检查，若逻辑突然反转，就说明掉进了同形近形词陷阱。

lessons.title: 多个状语怎样排列
lessons.meta: 方式、地点、时间与强调位置
examples: She sang beautifully on stage last night.
Yesterday, we worked quietly in the library.

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: 英语句尾常按“方式—地点—时间”排列；中文通常先交代时间和地点。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: 时间可移到句首作为背景；句尾仍让方式靠近动作、地点随后。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: carefully 放在动词前可突出动作方式；放句尾也自然，但焦点较平。

rules: 多个句尾状语的常见顺序是方式—地点—时间，但语境和信息焦点可以调整。
时间或地点状语可前置建立背景，前置后通常与主句用逗号隔开。
方式副词可放动词前或句尾；位置变化常改变强调重点，而非简单对错。

questions.question: Choose the neutral end order.

options.text: She spoke softly at home yesterday.
She spoke yesterday softly at home.

questions.correct: 中性句尾常按方式—地点—时间。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：中性句尾常按方式—地点—时间。

questions.question: Choose the natural background setting.

options.text: Last week, we met in Shanghai.
We last week met in Shanghai.

questions.correct: 时间状语可置于句首建立背景。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：时间状语可置于句首建立背景。

questions.question: 哪一句更突出“仔细地”这一方式？
questions.correct: 动词前位置更突出 carefully；两句都合语法。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：动词前位置更突出 carefully；两句都合语法。

narration.text:
一句话同时有“唱得很美、在舞台上、昨晚”，怎样排才不挤？中性说法是：<#0.4#>She sang beautifully on stage last night。<#0.8#>先交代方式 beautifully，再说地点 on stage，最后放时间 last night。这是多个句尾状语常见的“方式、地点、时间”顺序。
顺序不是铁板一块。<#0.4#>Yesterday, we worked quietly in the library。<#0.8#>Yesterday 被提到句首，先搭起昨天这个背景，后面再说怎样工作、在哪里工作。前置的时间或地点状语常与主句用逗号分开。<#0.7#>
She carefully opened the box 把 carefully 放在动词前，让“动作很小心”更早进入听者注意。这个句中位置强调的是方式，而前两句主要展示多个状语在句首和句尾怎样排布。
排列时先把每个状语标成方式、地点或时间；都放句尾时先试方式、地点、时间；若某个信息要承接上文或搭背景，就把它前置并加逗号；最后朗读检查，避免把方式副词硬塞到动词与宾语之间。

lessons.title: 句子副词表达什么态度
lessons.meta: 把握程度、评价与说话方式

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Perhaps 限定整句的真实性，表示说话人不完全确定。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately 不是说明“受伤得幸运”，而是评价“无人受伤”这件事是幸运的。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Frankly 表示“坦率地说”，说明说话人以什么态度表达整句话。

rules: perhaps、probably、certainly 等表示说话人对整句话真实性的把握程度。
fortunately、surprisingly、sadly 等评价整件事。
frankly、honestly、briefly 等可说明说话方式或组织话语。

questions.question: ___, the train may be late.
questions.correct: Perhaps 表示对整句的可能性判断。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Perhaps 表示对整句的可能性判断。

questions.question: ___, everyone escaped safely.
questions.correct: Fortunately 评价整件事的结果。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Fortunately 评价整件事的结果。

questions.question: ___, I do not support the plan.
questions.correct: Frankly 表示“坦率地说”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Frankly 表示“坦率地说”。

narration.text:
同一句 Mia is right，前面换一个副词，说话人的态度就变了。<#0.4#>Perhaps, Mia is right。<#0.8#>perhaps 表示“可能”，不是说明 Mia 怎样做事，而是降低说话人对整件判断的把握。
再看：<#0.4#>Fortunately, nobody was hurt。<#0.8#>nobody was hurt 是事实内容；Fortunately 表示说话人认为这个结果很幸运。这类词不是描写某一个动作，而是在评价整件事。<#0.7#>
Frankly, I disagree 里的 Frankly 也不是说“不同意得很坦率”，而是说明接下来这句话是坦率地讲出来。honestly、briefly 等还能提示说话方式或组织话语。
识别时先把句首副词拿掉，看剩下的主干事实是否完整；再问它表达的是对事实真假的把握、对结果的评价，还是讲话方式。perhaps、probably 属于把握程度，fortunately、sadly 属于评价，frankly、briefly 属于话语态度。别把它们误当成只修饰紧邻的主语。

lessons.title: 疑问副词与关系副词
lessons.meta: 询问或连接时间、地点、原因与方式
examples: This is the place where we met.
Tell me how you solved it.

analyses.label: 关系副词引导的定语从句

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Why 在句中询问 leave 的原因，不代替主语或宾语。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: where 在从句中表示“在这个地方”，连接 place 和 we met；中文通常译为“我们见面的地方”。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: how 在从句中询问 solved 的方式，整个 how 从句作 tell 的直接宾语。

rules: when、where、why、how 可作疑问副词，询问时间、地点、原因或方式。
when、where、why 可作关系副词，在从句中承担状语功能并连接先行词。
疑问副词也可引导名词性从句；此时整个从句占主语、宾语或表语位置。

questions.question: ___ did the meeting end?
questions.correct: When 询问结束时间。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：When 询问结束时间。

questions.question: I remember the day ___ we met.
questions.correct: when 在从句中作时间状语并连接 day。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：when 在从句中作时间状语并连接 day。

questions.question: Do you know ___ he left?
questions.correct: why 引导宾语从句并询问原因。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：why 引导宾语从句并询问原因。

narration.text:
why、where、how 都能出现在句首，但它们做的事不总一样。直接问离开的原因：<#0.4#>Why did you leave?<#0.8#>Why 是疑问副词，在疑问句中留下“因为什么”的空位，并触发主句疑问语序。
再看地点：<#0.4#>This is the place where we met。<#0.8#>where 不在提问，而是把 we met 接到先行词 place 上，并在从句里表示见面的地点。它既连接名词和定语从句，又在从句内作地点状语，所以叫关系副词。<#0.7#>
Tell me how you solved it 里，how 保留“怎样”的意义，引出一整块“你怎样解决它”的内容，整体作 tell 的宾语。这是疑问副词引导名词性从句，内部要用 you solved 的陈述语序。
判断时先看整句是不是直接提问；是，就按疑问副词处理。若前面有 time、place、reason 等先行词，后面从句在修饰它，就看关系副词；若从句整体回答“告诉、知道、询问什么”，就按名词性从句处理。最后检查它在从句内表示时间、地点、原因还是方式。

lessons.title: 否定与限制副词
examples: Never have I seen such a view.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: hardly 不是“努力地”，而是把 know 限定为“几乎不了解”，带近乎否定意义。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: rarely 表示事情发生频率极低，语义接近否定，但句中不再加 not。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: Never 前置加强否定后，助动词 have 移到主语 I 前形成部分倒装。

rules: hardly、scarcely、barely 表示“几乎不”，本身带近乎否定意义。
rarely、seldom 表示低频，通常不再与 not 重复否定。
否定或限制副词置于句首时，正式语体中常触发助动词与主语部分倒装。

questions.question: I can ___ hear you.
questions.correct: hardly 表示“几乎听不见”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：hardly 表示“几乎听不见”。

questions.question: She ___ eats fast food.
questions.correct: rarely 已表示低频近否定。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：rarely 已表示低频近否定。

questions.question: Never ___ such a view.
questions.correct: Never 前置触发助动词倒装。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Never 前置触发助动词倒装。

narration.text:
hardly 看起来像 hard 加 ly，意思却不是“努力地”。<#0.4#>I hardly know him。<#0.8#>hardly 表示“几乎不”，句子已经接近否定，不能再随手加 not 变成重复否定。
再听：<#0.4#>She rarely complains。<#0.8#>rarely 表示抱怨发生得很少，和 seldom 一样带低频限制。它们不是完全的 no，但已把发生频率压得很低，普通标准英语通常不再和 not 叠用。<#0.7#>
把否定或限制词推到句首，语序还会变化。Never have I seen such a view 先强调“从来没有”，随后把助动词 have 放到主语 I 前，形成部分倒装。这个倒装是句首否定范围带来的正式结构。
操作时先识别 hardly、scarcely、barely、rarely、seldom、never 自带的否定或限制强度；再圈出它们否定的是动作、频率还是范围；若它们位于句首，检查是否需要“助动词加主语加主要动词”的部分倒装。最后删掉没有特殊语境支撑的重复 not。

lessons.title: 连接副词怎样连接分句
examples: The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.
The task was difficult; however, we finished it.
First, check the data; then, write the report.

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: therefore 表示前因后果，但不能像 so 一样只用逗号连接两个独立分句。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: however 表示转折；前面用分号结束第一分句，后面用逗号隔开连接副词。

exampleNotes.title: 规则观察
exampleNotes.body: First 和 then 组织步骤顺序，连接的是信息推进关系。

rules: therefore、thus、consequently 表示结果；however、nevertheless 表示转折。
连接副词不是并列连词；连接两个独立分句时，前面通常用分号或句号，后面常用逗号。
first、then、meanwhile、finally 等可组织顺序和信息推进。

questions.question: The shop was closed; ___, we went home.
questions.correct: therefore 表示前句原因带来的结果。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：therefore 表示前句原因带来的结果。

questions.question: Choose the correct punctuation.
questions.correct: 两个独立分句间用分号，however 后用逗号。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：两个独立分句间用分号，however 后用逗号。

questions.question: ___, read the question; then answer it.
questions.correct: First 和 then 组织步骤顺序。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：First 和 then 组织步骤顺序。

narration.text:
道路封闭，我们换了路线，两件事之间是结果关系。英语可以写：<#0.4#>The road was closed; therefore, we took another route。<#0.8#>therefore 告诉读者后句是前句的结果，但它不是 and、so 那样的并列连词，不能只靠一个逗号把两个完整分句粘起来。这里先用分号结束第一层句界，therefore 后再加逗号。
转折也一样：<#0.4#>The task was difficult; however, we finished it。<#0.8#>however 标出“虽然困难，仍然完成”的反向关系。前面也可以直接用句号，写成两个句子。<#0.7#>
连接副词还能组织顺序。First, check the data; then, write the report 中，First 和 then 帮读者按步骤推进，不是连接两个词或短语。
判断时先看前后是不是各自完整的分句；再辨认副词标的是结果、转折还是顺序。如果用 therefore、however 等连接两个独立分句，前面选分号或句号，后面通常加逗号；不要写成“完整句，however 完整句”的逗号拼接。

en.title: Adverbs · 16 lessons
en.copy: Master the core rules, then handle complex contexts.

course.title: Definition and core of adverbs
course.meta: Add circumstances or scope to actions, qualities or clauses
examples: Probably, the train will arrive soon.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: calmly does not change the event of answering; it adds how the event happens.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: very does not describe the water directly; it raises the degree of cold.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Probably does not modify one word; it marks the speaker’s judgment about the whole event.

rules: An adverb adds time, place, manner, degree, frequency, stance or scope to an action, quality, another adverb or clause.
Do not identify an adverb by -ly alone; identify what it modifies and what information it adds.
Position often signals scope: an adverb normally relates most directly to the element it stands near.

questions.question: What does calmly add in “Mia answered calmly”?
questions.correct: calmly gives the manner of answering.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: calmly gives the manner of answering.

questions.question: What does very modify in “very cold”?
questions.correct: very directly modifies the degree of cold.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: very directly modifies the degree of cold.

questions.question: What does initial Probably normally scope over?
questions.correct: Probably marks probability for the whole clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Probably marks probability for the whole clause.

narration.text:
只说“米娅回答了”，事情已经完整；如果加上“平静地”，我们就知道她是怎么回答的。这个后来补上的词，不负责说人或东西“什么样”，而是在给动作加细节。这样的词常常叫副词。副词还能给一个性质加程度，甚至表达说话人对整件事的态度。<#0.8#>
先听。<#0.4#>Mia answered calmly。<#0.8#>主干只是 Mia answered。calmly 回答“怎么回答”，给动作 answered 加上方式。在句子里，这份补充方式的工作叫状语。<#0.8#>
再听。<#0.4#>The water is very cold。<#0.8#>very 不是在说明 water，也不是在说明 is，它只把 cold 的程度往上推，变成“非常冷”。所以副词不只跟动作，也可以跟形容词。<#0.8#>
再听一句。<#0.4#>Probably, the train will arrive soon。<#0.8#>soon 只告诉我们什么时候到；Probably 管的是整件事，表示说话人觉得“可能会到”。两个词都属于副词，管的范围却不一样。去掉 Probably，火车到达这件事还在，只是说话人的把握没有说出来。<#0.7#>
判断时别看到 ly 就直接下结论，因为 friendly 不是这里说的副词，fast 也没有 ly。先问这个词在给哪个动作、哪种性质或哪件事加信息；再问加的是时间、方式、程度还是态度；最后用整句意思检查它到底管到哪里。

course.title: What adverbs do
course.meta: Modify verbs, adjectives, adverbs or clauses
examples: He finished the task remarkably quickly.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: politely directly modifies answered and gives the manner of answering.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: very modifies the adjective cold and changes only its degree.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately evaluates the whole event, while safely gives the manner of arriving.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: remarkably modifies quickly, which in turn modifies finished.

rules: An adverb can modify a verb, for example to show manner.
A degree adverb can modify an adjective.
A degree adverb can also modify another adverb.
A sentence adverb can comment on or qualify a whole clause.

questions.question: She spoke ___.
questions.correct: clearly modifies the verb spoke.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: clearly modifies the verb spoke.

questions.question: The test is ___ easy.
questions.correct: quite is a degree adverb modifying easy.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: quite is a degree adverb modifying easy.

questions.question: ___, nobody was hurt.
questions.correct: Luckily comments on the whole clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Luckily comments on the whole clause.

questions.question: She completed the work extremely ___.
questions.correct: extremely modifies the adverb carefully, which modifies completed.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: extremely modifies the adverb carefully, which modifies completed.

narration.text:
同样是副词，作用目标可能完全不同。先听：<#0.4#>Mia answered politely。<#0.8#>主干 Mia answered 已经说明她回答了，politely 只补充“怎样回答”，直接修饰动词 answered。
再听：<#0.4#>The water is very cold。<#0.8#>very 不说明 water，也不说明 is，它只把 cold 的程度提高，所以修饰形容词。<#0.7#>
Fortunately, everyone arrived safely 里有两个副词。safely 只说明 arrived 的方式；Fortunately 表示说话人觉得“幸好大家安全到达”，评价的是整件事。把 Fortunately 去掉，事件仍在，只是说话人的态度没了。He finished the task remarkably quickly 中，quickly 说明完成得怎样，remarkably 再加强 quickly，形成“非常快地”。一个副词也能修饰另一个副词。
判断副词的工作，先别只找 ly。给副词画一根箭头：指向动作，就是修饰动词；指向性质词，就是修饰形容词；指向另一个方式或程度词，就是修饰副词；若它在评价整句话的可能性、幸运与否或说话态度，就按句子副词处理。

course.title: Adverbs versus adverbials
course.meta: A word class is not a sentence role
examples: She spoke in a soft voice.
She spoke when the room became quiet.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: softly is an adverb by word class and a manner adverbial by sentence function.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: in a soft voice is an adverbial, but its form is a prepositional phrase, not an adverb.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: The when-clause gives the time and functions as an adverbial; the clause itself is not an adverb.

rules: An adverb is a word class; an adverbial is a sentence function.
Adverbs can be adverbials, but prepositional, noun and non-finite phrases can also fill that function.
A clause can function as an adverbial of time, reason, condition, concession and more.

questions.question: What word class is softly?
questions.correct: softly is an adverb and can function as an adverbial.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: softly is an adverb and can function as an adverbial.

questions.question: Is “in the morning” an adverb?

options.text: No; it is a prepositional phrase.
Yes; every adverbial is an adverb.

questions.correct: It functions as an adverbial but is a prepositional phrase in form.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It functions as an adverbial but is a prepositional phrase in form.

questions.question: What is “when he arrived” as a whole?
questions.correct: It is a clause functioning as an adverbial.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It is a clause functioning as an adverbial.

narration.text:
老师问“softly 是副词还是状语”，答案可能是：两个说法都对，但回答的不是同一个问题。<#0.4#>She spoke softly。<#0.8#>softly 这个单词属于副词；它在句中回答“怎样说话”，承担的工作叫方式状语。副词是词的类别，状语是句子里的职位。
这个职位不只给副词坐。<#0.4#>She spoke in a soft voice。<#0.8#>in a soft voice 是介词短语，不是一个副词，但整块仍回答“怎样说话”，所以也作方式状语。<#0.7#>
She spoke when the room became quiet 中，when the room became quiet 里面有自己的主语和谓语，是一个从句；它整体回答“什么时候说话”，作时间状语。名词短语、非谓语短语也可能承担状语工作。
区分时分两层检查：先看形式，一个词是什么词类，一组词是介词短语、名词短语还是从句；再看功能，它对主句补充时间、地点、方式、原因还是条件。看到副词可以判断它常作状语，但看到状语绝不能反推它一定是副词。

course.title: Types of adverbs

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: English commonly places place before time; Chinese more often puts the time expression before the place expression.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: often gives frequency, quietly manner and here place; each answers a different question.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: too marks the degree of heavy as beyond an acceptable limit.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately evaluates the event, while soon gives the time of stopping.

rules: Time adverbs say when an action happens.
Place adverbs say where an action happens or points.
Manner adverbs say how an action happens.
Frequency adverbs say how often an action happens.
Degree adverbs express the degree of a quality, state or action.
Comment adverbs express the speaker’s attitude or judgment toward a whole clause.

questions.question: We met ___ yesterday.
questions.correct: there is a place adverb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: there is a place adverb.

questions.question: He ___ walks to school.
questions.correct: usually is a frequency adverb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: usually is a frequency adverb.

questions.question: The box is ___ small.
questions.correct: quite is a degree adverb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: quite is a degree adverb.

questions.question: We will leave ___.
questions.correct: tomorrow is a time adverb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: tomorrow is a time adverb.

questions.question: She answered ___.
questions.correct: politely is a manner adverb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: politely is a manner adverb.

questions.question: ___, the key was still there.
questions.correct: Luckily is a comment adverb modifying the whole clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Luckily is a comment adverb modifying the whole clause.

narration.text:
一句话里可能同时塞进好几种背景。<#0.4#>We will meet outside tomorrow。<#0.8#>outside 回答“在哪里见”，是地点副词；tomorrow 回答“什么时候见”，是时间副词。分类不是看它们站在句尾，而是看各自补了什么信息。
再听：<#0.4#>She often reads quietly here。<#0.8#>often 说明阅读发生得多频繁，是频率副词；quietly 回答“怎样读”，是方式副词；here 指出地点。三个词都和 reads 有关，却各自回答不同问题。<#0.7#>
The bag is too heavy 中，too 不说明时间地点，而是把 heavy 推到“过于重”的程度，叫程度副词。Fortunately, the rain stopped soon 里，soon 给 stopped 加时间；Fortunately 则评价“雨停了”整件事，表达说话人的态度。
分类时先找副词的作用对象，再逐个提问：何时是时间，何地是地点，怎样是方式，多常是频率，到什么程度是程度；若它表达对整件事的幸运、意外或把握，就归入评注性句子副词。一个句子可以同时出现多类，不必只选一个。

course.title: Forming adverbs

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Many manner adverbs add -ly to an adjective: quick becomes quickly.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: After consonant + y, normally change y to i before adding -ly.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: true drops e in truly; whole to wholly is another spelling to note.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: fast functions as an adverb without -ly; not all adverbs end in -ly.

rules: Many manner adverbs are formed by adding -ly to adjectives.
Consonant + y normally changes y to i before -ly.
Some forms have special spelling, such as true–truly, whole–wholly and full–fully.
fast, hard, late and early can be flat adverbs; an -ly form may have a different meaning.

questions.question: What is the adverb from careful?
questions.correct: careful adds -ly to form carefully.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: careful adds -ly to form carefully.

questions.question: What is the adverb from happy?
questions.correct: Change y to i before -ly.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Change y to i before -ly.

questions.question: What is the adverb from true?
questions.correct: true drops e to form truly.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: true drops e to form truly.

questions.question: He works ___.
questions.correct: hard means “with effort”; hardly means “almost not”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: hard means “with effort”; hardly means “almost not”.

narration.text:
想把 quick 变成“快速地”，最常见的办法是加 ly：<#0.4#>quick → quickly。<#0.8#>但不能只在每个形容词后面随手粘 ly，拼写和词义都要检查。
第二组是 happy → happily。happy 结尾是辅音字母加 y，变副词时先把 y 改成 i，再加 ly。<#0.7#>第三组 true → truly，要去掉结尾的 e，再加 ly。这些变化说明构词还要处理原词拼写。<#0.7#>
最后看 He runs fast。fast 没有 ly，却直接修饰 runs，说明动作怎样发生。不是所有副词都以 ly 结尾，也不是所有形容词都必须加 ly 才能承担副词功能。
构词时先确认句中真的需要副词；普通方式词可尝试加 ly；遇到辅音加 y、true、full 等词先处理拼写；最后检查这个词是否本来就能同形作副词，以及 ly 形式有没有产生新意思。不能用“有 ly 就是副词、没 ly 就不是”来判断。

course.title: Where adverbs go
examples: Yesterday, we finished the work quickly.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: usually precedes the main verb walks and gives its frequency.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: With be, always follows is and precedes the complement kind.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Yesterday sets the time first; quickly at the end gives the manner of finishing.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: never follows the first auxiliary has and precedes the main verb visited.

rules: Frequency adverbs normally precede main verbs.
Frequency adverbs normally follow be.
With auxiliaries, a frequency adverb normally follows the first auxiliary.
A manner adverb often follows the verb and its object.
A time adverb may come first or last; a fronted time adverb is commonly followed by a comma.

questions.question: Tom ___ gets up early.
questions.correct: often normally comes before the main verb gets.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: often normally comes before the main verb gets.

questions.question: She is ___ late.
questions.correct: A frequency adverb follows be.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A frequency adverb follows be.

questions.question: He completed the task ___.
questions.correct: The manner adverb carefully naturally follows the object.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The manner adverb carefully naturally follows the object.

questions.question: She has ___ seen snow.
questions.correct: never follows the first auxiliary has.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: never follows the first auxiliary has.

questions.question: Choose the natural time-adverb position.
questions.correct: A time adverb can be fronted and followed by a comma.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A time adverb can be fronted and followed by a comma.

narration.text:
你想说 Lily 通常走路上学，usually 放哪儿？英语说：<#0.4#>Lily usually walks to school。<#0.8#>walks 是实义动词，频率副词通常站在它前面。
换成 be，位置就换了：<#0.4#>Lily is always kind。<#0.8#>always 放在 is 后。第三句 Yesterday, we finished the work quickly 把时间提到句首作背景，让方式副词 quickly 放在动词和宾语之后。<#0.7#>
最后看 She has never visited London。句中有助动词 has，never 放在第一个助动词后、主要动词 visited 前。可以把频率副词想成靠近谓语核心的中间位置，但具体落点要看前面是 be 还是助动词。
操作时先给副词分类。频率词遇到实义动词放前，遇到 be 放后，有助动词放第一个助动词后；方式词通常放动词和宾语之后；时间词可放句首或句尾，句首背景后常加逗号。最后再按想强调的信息作小幅调整。

course.title: Ordering multiple adverbials
examples: She sang beautifully on stage last night.
Yesterday, we worked quietly in the library.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: English end position often follows manner–place–time; Chinese commonly gives time and place earlier.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Time moves first as the setting; manner stays close to the action and place follows.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: carefully before the verb gives manner more focus; end position is also natural but less marked.

rules: A common end order is manner–place–time, though context and focus can change it.
A time or place adverbial can be fronted as a setting and is normally followed by a comma.
A manner adverb can occur before the verb or at the end; the position often changes focus rather than grammaticality.

questions.question: Choose the neutral end order.

options.text: She spoke softly at home yesterday.
She spoke yesterday softly at home.

questions.correct: Neutral end order commonly follows manner–place–time.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Neutral end order commonly follows manner–place–time.

questions.question: Choose the natural background setting.

options.text: Last week, we met in Shanghai.
We last week met in Shanghai.

questions.correct: A fronted time adverbial establishes the setting.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A fronted time adverbial establishes the setting.

questions.question: Which sentence gives more focus to carefully?
questions.correct: Preverbal position gives carefully more focus; both are grammatical.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Preverbal position gives carefully more focus; both are grammatical.

narration.text:
一句话同时有“唱得很美、在舞台上、昨晚”，怎样排才不挤？中性说法是：<#0.4#>She sang beautifully on stage last night。<#0.8#>先交代方式 beautifully，再说地点 on stage，最后放时间 last night。这是多个句尾状语常见的“方式、地点、时间”顺序。
顺序不是铁板一块。<#0.4#>Yesterday, we worked quietly in the library。<#0.8#>Yesterday 被提到句首，先搭起昨天这个背景，后面再说怎样工作、在哪里工作。前置的时间或地点状语常与主句用逗号分开。<#0.7#>
She carefully opened the box 把 carefully 放在动词前，让“动作很小心”更早进入听者注意。这个句中位置强调的是方式，而前两句主要展示多个状语在句首和句尾怎样排布。
排列时先把每个状语标成方式、地点或时间；都放句尾时先试方式、地点、时间；若某个信息要承接上文或搭背景，就把它前置并加逗号；最后朗读检查，避免把方式副词硬塞到动词与宾语之间。

course.title: Adjective or adverb?
course.meta: Linking verbs, action verbs and flat adverbs
examples: The child smelled the flower carefully.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: smell is linking, so sweet describes the flowers as an adjective.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: smelled is an action, and carefully gives its manner as an adverb.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: fast keeps the same form but modifies moves here, so it is an adverb.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: friendly ends in -ly but describes neighbour, so it is an adjective complement.

rules: Use an adjective after a linking verb to describe the subject.
Use an adverb to modify an action verb.
fast, hard, late and early can be adverbs without -ly.
friendly and lovely end in -ly but are normally adjectives.

questions.question: The music sounds ___.
questions.correct: sound is linking here and takes an adjective.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: sound is linking here and takes an adjective.

questions.question: She sings ___.
questions.correct: beautifully modifies the action verb sings.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: beautifully modifies the action verb sings.

questions.question: He works ___.
questions.correct: hard is an adverb here meaning “with effort”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: hard is an adverb here meaning “with effort”.

questions.question: She gave me a ___ smile.
questions.correct: friendly is an adjective modifying smile.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: friendly is an adjective modifying smile.

narration.text:
闻到花香时，英语说：<#0.4#>The flowers smell sweet。<#0.8#>这里 smell 是“闻起来”，像一座桥把 flowers 和 sweet 连起来。sweet 说明花本身的性质，所以在这里是形容词。
如果孩子主动去闻花，句子变成：<#0.4#>The child smelled the flower carefully。<#0.8#>smelled 现在是行为动作，carefully 回答孩子“怎样闻”，所以用副词。判断形式前，要先分清动词是在连接主语状态，还是在表示真实动作。<#0.7#>
词尾也会骗人。The train moves fast 里，fast 没有 ly，却直接说明 moves 的方式。Our new neighbour is friendly 中，friendly 虽然以 ly 结尾，却通过 is 说明 neighbour，所以是形容词。
选择时先问被说明的是人或物的状态，还是动作发生的方式。系动词后说明主语，用形容词；行为动词旁说明动作，通常用副词。接着检查例句中的 fast 和 friendly 这类形式，不能只靠 ly 词尾下结论。

course.title: Comparing adverbs
examples: Ben answered more carefully than I did.
Of all the runners, Leo ran the fastest.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: faster compares the manner or speed of running and modifies runs.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: carefully is an -ly adverb, so its comparative uses more.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: of all the runners defines a group of three or more, so the adverb superlative is used.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: better is the irregular comparative of well and compares the performance with before.

rules: Short adverbs often add -er/-est to form comparatives and superlatives.
Most -ly adverbs form comparison with more/most.
Forms such as well–better–best and badly–worse–worst are irregular.

questions.question: Jane speaks ___ than before.
questions.correct: An -ly adverb normally forms its comparative with more.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: An -ly adverb normally forms its comparative with more.

questions.question: Tom runs ___ of the three.
questions.correct: Use the adverb superlative for a group of three.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use the adverb superlative for a group of three.

questions.question: She did ___ than yesterday.
questions.correct: better is the irregular comparative of well.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: better is the irregular comparative of well.

narration.text:
比赛时不只比较谁更高，还会比较谁跑得更快。<#0.4#>Amy runs faster than Sue。<#0.8#>faster 说明动作 runs 的速度更高。fast 是短副词，比较级直接加 er，最高级加 est。
若副词以 ly 结尾，通常不把词拉得更长。<#0.4#>Ben answered more carefully than I did。<#0.8#>carefully 前加 more 表示更仔细；三者以上可用 most carefully。Of all the runners, Leo ran the fastest 画出多人范围，用 fastest 选出速度最高者。<#0.7#>
还有不规则形式。Nora performed better than before 中，better 是 well 的比较级；well、better、best 要整体记。badly 则变 worse、worst。
操作时先确认比较的是动作方式或程度，而不是人或物的性质；再看副词形式。短副词常加 er 或 est，多数 ly 副词用 more 或 most；最后检查 well、badly 等不规则变化，并用 than 或范围短语说清比较基准。

course.title: Degree adverb patterns
examples: The room is warm enough for the baby.
The box is too heavy for me to lift.
It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it.
The question was so difficult that nobody answered it.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: enough follows warm and marks the degree as sufficient for the baby.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: too precedes heavy and marks a degree beyond what I can lift.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: such modifies the noun phrase a difficult question, and the that-clause gives the result.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: so directly modifies difficult, and the that-clause gives the result.

rules: enough follows the adjective or adverb it modifies.
too precedes an adjective or adverb and often means “excessively...to...”.
so modifies an adjective or adverb, as in so difficult.
such modifies a noun phrase, as in such a difficult task.

questions.question: She is old ___ to travel alone.
questions.correct: enough follows the adjective it modifies.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: enough follows the adjective it modifies.

questions.question: The water is ___ hot to drink.
questions.correct: too...to means excessively hot to drink.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: too...to means excessively hot to drink.

questions.question: It was ___ an exciting match.
questions.correct: Use such before the noun phrase an exciting match.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use such before the noun phrase an exciting match.

questions.question: The film was ___ exciting that we watched it twice.
questions.correct: exciting is an adjective, so use so.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: exciting is an adjective, so use so.

narration.text:
同样是“很暖”，几个程度词站的位置不一样。宝宝待在房间里刚好合适，可以说：<#0.4#>The room is warm enough for the baby。<#0.8#>enough 放在形容词 warm 后，表示程度已经足够。
箱子重到我抬不动，就说：<#0.4#>The box is too heavy for me to lift。<#0.8#>too 放在 heavy 前，表示程度超过合适范围，后面的 for me to lift 说明对谁、做什么来说太重。<#0.7#>
第三句 It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it 中，such 抓住整个名词短语 a difficult question。第四句 The question was so difficult that nobody answered it 里，so 直接修饰形容词 difficult。两句结果相同，程度词后面的结构不同。
选择时先看程度词后面的中心。修饰形容词或副词，enough 放后面，too 和 so 放前面；修饰带冠词和名词的整块，用 such。若后面还有 that 从句，再判断前面突出的是性质程度，还是包含冠词、形容词和名词的完整名词短语。

course.title: Adverb scope changes meaning
examples: Even Ben almost missed the bus.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: Only Mia means Mia and nobody else; the position of only determines its focus.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: only solved focuses on the action and differs from Only Mia.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Even focuses Ben as unexpected; almost modifies missed and means the event nearly happened.

rules: only should stand near its focus; a position change can alter meaning.
even marks an unexpected focus.
almost says an event came close to happening but did not.

questions.question: Which sentence means that Li Hua—and nobody else—passed the exam?

options.text: Only Li Hua passed the exam.
Li Hua only passed the exam.

questions.correct: only next to Li Hua focuses on who passed.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: only next to Li Hua focuses on who passed.

questions.question: She ___ missed the bus; she arrived just in time.
questions.correct: almost missed means it nearly happened but did not.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: almost missed means it nearly happened but did not.

questions.question: ___ Ben understood the difficult puzzle.
questions.correct: Even focuses Ben and marks the result as unexpected.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Even focuses Ben and marks the result as unexpected.

narration.text:
一句话只挪动 only，重点就可能换人。<#0.4#>Only Mia solved the puzzle。<#0.8#>only 靠近 Mia，排除的是其他人：只有米娅解开了。第二句 Mia only solved the puzzle 中，only 靠近 solved，更容易表示她只是解开了，没有做别的。副词影响哪一块内容，叫作用范围；位置常在帮我们标范围。<#0.7#>
最后看 Even Ben almost missed the bus。even 把 Ben 标成出乎意料的人，暗示连他都差点误车；almost 修饰 missed，表示事情接近发生，但最后没有真的错过。两个副词在同一句里，各有自己的焦点。<#0.7#>
判断时给 only、even、almost 各画一条括号，圈住它最直接限定的成分；再用排除、意外或接近发生来改述意思。若一句话可能圈出两种范围，就把副词挪到目标成分旁边，或改写句子，让焦点唯一。

course.title: What sentence adverbs express

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Perhaps scopes over the whole claim and shows uncertainty.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately does not describe how anyone was hurt; it evaluates the whole outcome as fortunate.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Frankly means “speaking frankly” and frames the speaker’s stance toward the statement.

rules: perhaps, probably and certainly mark the speaker’s degree of certainty about a clause.
fortunately, surprisingly and sadly evaluate the whole event.
frankly, honestly and briefly can frame the manner of speaking or discourse organization.

questions.question: ___, the train may be late.
questions.correct: Perhaps marks possibility for the whole clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Perhaps marks possibility for the whole clause.

questions.question: ___, everyone escaped safely.
questions.correct: Fortunately evaluates the outcome.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Fortunately evaluates the outcome.

questions.question: ___, I do not support the plan.
questions.correct: Frankly frames the statement as frank speech.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Frankly frames the statement as frank speech.

narration.text:
同一句 Mia is right，前面换一个副词，说话人的态度就变了。<#0.4#>Perhaps, Mia is right。<#0.8#>perhaps 表示“可能”，不是说明 Mia 怎样做事，而是降低说话人对整件判断的把握。
再看：<#0.4#>Fortunately, nobody was hurt。<#0.8#>nobody was hurt 是事实内容；Fortunately 表示说话人认为这个结果很幸运。这类词不是描写某一个动作，而是在评价整件事。<#0.7#>
Frankly, I disagree 里的 Frankly 也不是说“不同意得很坦率”，而是说明接下来这句话是坦率地讲出来。honestly、briefly 等还能提示说话方式或组织话语。
识别时先把句首副词拿掉，看剩下的主干事实是否完整；再问它表达的是对事实真假的把握、对结果的评价，还是讲话方式。perhaps、probably 属于把握程度，fortunately、sadly 属于评价，frankly、briefly 属于话语态度。别把它们误当成只修饰紧邻的主语。

course.title: Interrogative and relative adverbs
course.meta: Ask or link time, place, reason and manner
examples: This is the place where we met.
Tell me how you solved it.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Why asks for the reason for leaving; it does not replace a subject or object.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: where means “at this place” in the clause and links it to place.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: how asks for the manner of solving; the whole how-clause is the direct object of tell.

rules: when, where, why and how can be interrogative adverbs asking about time, place, reason or manner.
when, where and why can be relative adverbs functioning adverbially while linking an antecedent.
An interrogative adverb can introduce a nominal clause that fills a subject, object or complement slot.

questions.question: ___ did the meeting end?
questions.correct: When asks about the time of ending.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: When asks about the time of ending.

questions.question: I remember the day ___ we met.
questions.correct: when functions as a time adverb and links day.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: when functions as a time adverb and links day.

questions.question: Do you know ___ he left?
questions.correct: why introduces an object clause asking for the reason.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: why introduces an object clause asking for the reason.

narration.text:
why、where、how 都能出现在句首，但它们做的事不总一样。直接问离开的原因：<#0.4#>Why did you leave?<#0.8#>Why 是疑问副词，在疑问句中留下“因为什么”的空位，并触发主句疑问语序。
再看地点：<#0.4#>This is the place where we met。<#0.8#>where 不在提问，而是把 we met 接到先行词 place 上，并在从句里表示见面的地点。它既连接名词和定语从句，又在从句内作地点状语，所以叫关系副词。<#0.7#>
Tell me how you solved it 里，how 保留“怎样”的意义，引出一整块“你怎样解决它”的内容，整体作 tell 的宾语。这是疑问副词引导名词性从句，内部要用 you solved 的陈述语序。
判断时先看整句是不是直接提问；是，就按疑问副词处理。若前面有 time、place、reason 等先行词，后面从句在修饰它，就看关系副词；若从句整体回答“告诉、知道、询问什么”，就按名词性从句处理。最后检查它在从句内表示时间、地点、原因还是方式。

course.title: Negative and limiting adverbs
examples: Never have I seen such a view.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: hardly does not mean “with effort”; it makes know nearly negative.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: rarely gives an extremely low frequency and is near-negative, so no extra not is used.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Fronted Never triggers partial inversion, moving have before I.

rules: hardly, scarcely and barely mean “almost not” and carry near-negative force.
rarely and seldom mark low frequency and normally do not combine with an extra not.
A fronted negative or limiting adverb often triggers subject–auxiliary inversion in formal style.

questions.question: I can ___ hear you.
questions.correct: hardly means “can almost not hear”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: hardly means “can almost not hear”.

questions.question: She ___ eats fast food.
questions.correct: rarely already carries low-frequency negative meaning.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: rarely already carries low-frequency negative meaning.

questions.question: Never ___ such a view.
questions.correct: Fronted Never triggers subject–auxiliary inversion.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Fronted Never triggers subject–auxiliary inversion.

narration.text:
hardly 看起来像 hard 加 ly，意思却不是“努力地”。<#0.4#>I hardly know him。<#0.8#>hardly 表示“几乎不”，句子已经接近否定，不能再随手加 not 变成重复否定。
再听：<#0.4#>She rarely complains。<#0.8#>rarely 表示抱怨发生得很少，和 seldom 一样带低频限制。它们不是完全的 no，但已把发生频率压得很低，普通标准英语通常不再和 not 叠用。<#0.7#>
把否定或限制词推到句首，语序还会变化。Never have I seen such a view 先强调“从来没有”，随后把助动词 have 放到主语 I 前，形成部分倒装。这个倒装是句首否定范围带来的正式结构。
操作时先识别 hardly、scarcely、barely、rarely、seldom、never 自带的否定或限制强度；再圈出它们否定的是动作、频率还是范围；若它们位于句首，检查是否需要“助动词加主语加主要动词”的部分倒装。最后删掉没有特殊语境支撑的重复 not。

course.title: How conjunctive adverbs link clauses
examples: The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.
The task was difficult; however, we finished it.
First, check the data; then, write the report.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: therefore marks result but cannot join two independent clauses with only a comma as so can.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: however marks contrast; a semicolon closes the first clause and a comma follows the adverb.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: First and then organize the sequence and progression of information.

rules: therefore, thus and consequently mark result; however and nevertheless mark contrast.
A conjunctive adverb is not a coordinator; between independent clauses it normally follows a semicolon or period and is followed by a comma.
first, then, meanwhile and finally organize sequence and information flow.

questions.question: The shop was closed; ___, we went home.
questions.correct: therefore marks the result of the first clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: therefore marks the result of the first clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct punctuation.
questions.correct: Use a semicolon between the clauses and a comma after however.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use a semicolon between the clauses and a comma after however.

questions.question: ___, read the question; then answer it.
questions.correct: First and then organize sequence.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: First and then organize sequence.

narration.text:
道路封闭，我们换了路线，两件事之间是结果关系。英语可以写：<#0.4#>The road was closed; therefore, we took another route。<#0.8#>therefore 告诉读者后句是前句的结果，但它不是 and、so 那样的并列连词，不能只靠一个逗号把两个完整分句粘起来。这里先用分号结束第一层句界，therefore 后再加逗号。
转折也一样：<#0.4#>The task was difficult; however, we finished it。<#0.8#>however 标出“虽然困难，仍然完成”的反向关系。前面也可以直接用句号，写成两个句子。<#0.7#>
连接副词还能组织顺序。First, check the data; then, write the report 中，First 和 then 帮读者按步骤推进，不是连接两个词或短语。
判断时先看前后是不是各自完整的分句；再辨认副词标的是结果、转折还是顺序。如果用 therefore、however 等连接两个独立分句，前面选分号或句号，后面通常加逗号；不要写成“完整句，however 完整句”的逗号拼接。

course.title: Easily confused adverbs
examples: I have hardly seen her lately.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: hard modifies works meaning “with effort”; hardly means “almost not”.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: hardly means almost never seen; lately means recently, not ordinary -ly forms of hard and late.

rules: hard means “with effort/intensely”, while hardly means “almost not”.
late means “after the expected time”, while lately means “recently”.

questions.question: She studies ___.
questions.correct: hard means “with effort”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: hard means “with effort”.

questions.question: Have you seen Tom ___?
questions.correct: lately means “recently”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: lately means “recently”.

narration.text:
有些副词只差两个字母，意思却拐到另一条路。<#0.4#>He works hard every day。<#0.8#>hard 修饰 works，表示“努力地”。如果换成 hardly，句子就变成“他几乎不工作”，不是“更努力”。
再听：<#0.4#>I have hardly seen her lately。<#0.8#>hardly 表示“几乎没见过”，lately 表示“最近”。这里两个 ly 形式都不能从 hard 和 late 的表面意思直接推出来。<#0.7#>
第二句同时放入 hardly 和 lately，正好展示 ly 形式可能形成独立词义。lately 只谈最近一段时间，不能按 late 的“迟”直接推导。类似词必须把整组意义分开存，而不是把 ly 当作普通构词尾。
遇到 hard 或 hardly，先问句子要表达努力，还是几乎不；遇到 late 或 lately，先问是某次到得迟，还是最近这段时间。选完后把中文意思完整代回原句检查，若逻辑突然反转，就说明掉进了同形近形词陷阱。

lessons.title: Definition and core of adverbs
lessons.meta: Add circumstances or scope to actions, qualities or clauses
examples: Probably, the train will arrive soon.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: calmly does not change the event of answering; it adds how the event happens.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: very does not describe the water directly; it raises the degree of cold.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Probably does not modify one word; it marks the speaker’s judgment about the whole event.

rules: An adverb adds time, place, manner, degree, frequency, stance or scope to an action, quality, another adverb or clause.
Do not identify an adverb by -ly alone; identify what it modifies and what information it adds.
Position often signals scope: an adverb normally relates most directly to the element it stands near.

questions.question: What does calmly add in “Mia answered calmly”?
questions.correct: calmly gives the manner of answering.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: calmly gives the manner of answering.

questions.question: What does very modify in “very cold”?
questions.correct: very directly modifies the degree of cold.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: very directly modifies the degree of cold.

questions.question: What does initial Probably normally scope over?

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Probably marks probability for the whole clause.

narration.text:
只说“米娅回答了”，事情已经完整；如果加上“平静地”，我们就知道她是怎么回答的。这个后来补上的词，不负责说人或东西“什么样”，而是在给动作加细节。这样的词常常叫副词。副词还能给一个性质加程度，甚至表达说话人对整件事的态度。<#0.8#>
先听。<#0.4#>Mia answered calmly。<#0.8#>主干只是 Mia answered。calmly 回答“怎么回答”，给动作 answered 加上方式。在句子里，这份补充方式的工作叫状语。<#0.8#>
再听。<#0.4#>The water is very cold。<#0.8#>very 不是在说明 water，也不是在说明 is，它只把 cold 的程度往上推，变成“非常冷”。所以副词不只跟动作，也可以跟形容词。<#0.8#>
再听一句。<#0.4#>Probably, the train will arrive soon。<#0.8#>soon 只告诉我们什么时候到；Probably 管的是整件事，表示说话人觉得“可能会到”。两个词都属于副词，管的范围却不一样。去掉 Probably，火车到达这件事还在，只是说话人的把握没有说出来。<#0.7#>
判断时别看到 ly 就直接下结论，因为 friendly 不是这里说的副词，fast 也没有 ly。先问这个词在给哪个动作、哪种性质或哪件事加信息；再问加的是时间、方式、程度还是态度；最后用整句意思检查它到底管到哪里。

lessons.title: What adverbs do
lessons.meta: Modify verbs, adjectives, adverbs or clauses
examples: He finished the task remarkably quickly.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: politely directly modifies answered and gives the manner of answering.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: very modifies the adjective cold and changes only its degree.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately evaluates the whole event, while safely gives the manner of arriving.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: remarkably modifies quickly, which in turn modifies finished.

rules: An adverb can modify a verb, for example to show manner.
A degree adverb can modify an adjective.
A degree adverb can also modify another adverb.
A sentence adverb can comment on or qualify a whole clause.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: clearly modifies the verb spoke.

questions.question: The test is ___ easy.
questions.correct: quite is a degree adverb modifying easy.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: quite is a degree adverb modifying easy.

questions.correct: Luckily comments on the whole clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Luckily comments on the whole clause.

questions.correct: extremely modifies the adverb carefully, which modifies completed.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: extremely modifies the adverb carefully, which modifies completed.

narration.text:
同样是副词，作用目标可能完全不同。先听：<#0.4#>Mia answered politely。<#0.8#>主干 Mia answered 已经说明她回答了，politely 只补充“怎样回答”，直接修饰动词 answered。
再听：<#0.4#>The water is very cold。<#0.8#>very 不说明 water，也不说明 is，它只把 cold 的程度提高，所以修饰形容词。<#0.7#>
Fortunately, everyone arrived safely 里有两个副词。safely 只说明 arrived 的方式；Fortunately 表示说话人觉得“幸好大家安全到达”，评价的是整件事。把 Fortunately 去掉，事件仍在，只是说话人的态度没了。He finished the task remarkably quickly 中，quickly 说明完成得怎样，remarkably 再加强 quickly，形成“非常快地”。一个副词也能修饰另一个副词。
判断副词的工作，先别只找 ly。给副词画一根箭头：指向动作，就是修饰动词；指向性质词，就是修饰形容词；指向另一个方式或程度词，就是修饰副词；若它在评价整句话的可能性、幸运与否或说话态度，就按句子副词处理。

lessons.title: Adverbs versus adverbials
lessons.meta: A word class is not a sentence role
examples: She spoke in a soft voice.

exampleNotes.body: softly is an adverb by word class and a manner adverbial by sentence function.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: in a soft voice is an adverbial, but its form is a prepositional phrase, not an adverb.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: The when-clause gives the time and functions as an adverbial; the clause itself is not an adverb.

rules: An adverb is a word class; an adverbial is a sentence function.
Adverbs can be adverbials, but prepositional, noun and non-finite phrases can also fill that function.
A clause can function as an adverbial of time, reason, condition, concession and more.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: softly is an adverb and can function as an adverbial.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: It functions as an adverbial but is a prepositional phrase in form.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: It is a clause functioning as an adverbial.

narration.text:
老师问“softly 是副词还是状语”，答案可能是：两个说法都对，但回答的不是同一个问题。<#0.4#>She spoke softly。<#0.8#>softly 这个单词属于副词；它在句中回答“怎样说话”，承担的工作叫方式状语。副词是词的类别，状语是句子里的职位。
这个职位不只给副词坐。<#0.4#>She spoke in a soft voice。<#0.8#>in a soft voice 是介词短语，不是一个副词，但整块仍回答“怎样说话”，所以也作方式状语。<#0.7#>
She spoke when the room became quiet 中，when the room became quiet 里面有自己的主语和谓语，是一个从句；它整体回答“什么时候说话”，作时间状语。名词短语、非谓语短语也可能承担状语工作。
区分时分两层检查：先看形式，一个词是什么词类，一组词是介词短语、名词短语还是从句；再看功能，它对主句补充时间、地点、方式、原因还是条件。看到副词可以判断它常作状语，但看到状语绝不能反推它一定是副词。

lessons.title: Types of adverbs

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: English commonly places place before time; Chinese more often puts the time expression before the place expression.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: often gives frequency, quietly manner and here place; each answers a different question.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: too marks the degree of heavy as beyond an acceptable limit.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Fortunately evaluates the event, while soon gives the time of stopping.

rules: Time adverbs say when an action happens.
Place adverbs say where an action happens or points.
Manner adverbs say how an action happens.
Frequency adverbs say how often an action happens.
Degree adverbs express the degree of a quality, state or action.
Comment adverbs express the speaker’s attitude or judgment toward a whole clause.

narration.text:
一句话里可能同时塞进好几种背景。<#0.4#>We will meet outside tomorrow。<#0.8#>outside 回答“在哪里见”，是地点副词；tomorrow 回答“什么时候见”，是时间副词。分类不是看它们站在句尾，而是看各自补了什么信息。
再听：<#0.4#>She often reads quietly here。<#0.8#>often 说明阅读发生得多频繁，是频率副词；quietly 回答“怎样读”，是方式副词；here 指出地点。三个词都和 reads 有关，却各自回答不同问题。<#0.7#>
The bag is too heavy 中，too 不说明时间地点，而是把 heavy 推到“过于重”的程度，叫程度副词。Fortunately, the rain stopped soon 里，soon 给 stopped 加时间；Fortunately 则评价“雨停了”整件事，表达说话人的态度。
分类时先找副词的作用对象，再逐个提问：何时是时间，何地是地点，怎样是方式，多常是频率，到什么程度是程度；若它表达对整件事的幸运、意外或把握，就归入评注性句子副词。一个句子可以同时出现多类，不必只选一个。

lessons.title: Forming adverbs

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Many manner adverbs add -ly to an adjective: quick becomes quickly.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: After consonant + y, normally change y to i before adding -ly.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: true drops e in truly; whole to wholly is another spelling to note.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: fast functions as an adverb without -ly; not all adverbs end in -ly.

rules: Many manner adverbs are formed by adding -ly to adjectives.
Consonant + y normally changes y to i before -ly.
Some forms have special spelling, such as true–truly, whole–wholly and full–fully.
fast, hard, late and early can be flat adverbs; an -ly form may have a different meaning.

questions.question: What is the adverb from careful?

questions.wrong: Check the rule: careful adds -ly to form carefully.

questions.question: What is the adverb from happy?

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Change y to i before -ly.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: true drops e to form truly.

questions.question: He works ___.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: hard means “with effort”; hardly means “almost not”.

narration.text:
想把 quick 变成“快速地”，最常见的办法是加 ly：<#0.4#>quick → quickly。<#0.8#>但不能只在每个形容词后面随手粘 ly，拼写和词义都要检查。
第二组是 happy → happily。happy 结尾是辅音字母加 y，变副词时先把 y 改成 i，再加 ly。<#0.7#>第三组 true → truly，要去掉结尾的 e，再加 ly。这些变化说明构词还要处理原词拼写。<#0.7#>
最后看 He runs fast。fast 没有 ly，却直接修饰 runs，说明动作怎样发生。不是所有副词都以 ly 结尾，也不是所有形容词都必须加 ly 才能承担副词功能。
构词时先确认句中真的需要副词；普通方式词可尝试加 ly；遇到辅音加 y、true、full 等词先处理拼写；最后检查这个词是否本来就能同形作副词，以及 ly 形式有没有产生新意思。不能用“有 ly 就是副词、没 ly 就不是”来判断。

lessons.title: Where adverbs go
examples: Yesterday, we finished the work quickly.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: With be, always follows is and precedes the complement kind.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: Yesterday sets the time first; quickly at the end gives the manner of finishing.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: never follows the first auxiliary has and precedes the main verb visited.

rules: Frequency adverbs normally precede main verbs.
Frequency adverbs normally follow be.
With auxiliaries, a frequency adverb normally follows the first auxiliary.
A manner adverb often follows the verb and its object.
A time adverb may come first or last; a fronted time adverb is commonly followed by a comma.

narration.text:
你想说 Lily 通常走路上学，usually 放哪儿？英语说：<#0.4#>Lily usually walks to school。<#0.8#>walks 是实义动词，频率副词通常站在它前面。
换成 be，位置就换了：<#0.4#>Lily is always kind。<#0.8#>always 放在 is 后。第三句 Yesterday, we finished the work quickly 把时间提到句首作背景，让方式副词 quickly 放在动词和宾语之后。<#0.7#>
最后看 She has never visited London。句中有助动词 has，never 放在第一个助动词后、主要动词 visited 前。可以把频率副词想成靠近谓语核心的中间位置，但具体落点要看前面是 be 还是助动词。
操作时先给副词分类。频率词遇到实义动词放前，遇到 be 放后，有助动词放第一个助动词后；方式词通常放动词和宾语之后；时间词可放句首或句尾，句首背景后常加逗号。最后再按想强调的信息作小幅调整。

lessons.title: Adjective or adverb?
lessons.meta: Linking verbs, action verbs and flat adverbs
examples: The child smelled the flower carefully.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: smell is linking, so sweet describes the flowers as an adjective.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: smelled is an action, and carefully gives its manner as an adverb.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: fast keeps the same form but modifies moves here, so it is an adverb.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: friendly ends in -ly but describes neighbour, so it is an adjective complement.

rules: Use an adjective after a linking verb to describe the subject.
Use an adverb to modify an action verb.
fast, hard, late and early can be adverbs without -ly.
friendly and lovely end in -ly but are normally adjectives.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: sound is linking here and takes an adjective.

narration.text:
闻到花香时，英语说：<#0.4#>The flowers smell sweet。<#0.8#>这里 smell 是“闻起来”，像一座桥把 flowers 和 sweet 连起来。sweet 说明花本身的性质，所以在这里是形容词。
如果孩子主动去闻花，句子变成：<#0.4#>The child smelled the flower carefully。<#0.8#>smelled 现在是行为动作，carefully 回答孩子“怎样闻”，所以用副词。判断形式前，要先分清动词是在连接主语状态，还是在表示真实动作。<#0.7#>
词尾也会骗人。The train moves fast 里，fast 没有 ly，却直接说明 moves 的方式。Our new neighbour is friendly 中，friendly 虽然以 ly 结尾，却通过 is 说明 neighbour，所以是形容词。

examples: Ben answered more carefully than I did.
Of all the runners, Leo ran the fastest.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: faster compares the manner or speed of running and modifies runs.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: of all the runners defines a group of three or more, so the adverb superlative is used.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: better is the irregular comparative of well and compares the performance with before.

rules: Short adverbs often add -er/-est to form comparatives and superlatives.
Most -ly adverbs form comparison with more/most.
Forms such as well–better–best and badly–worse–worst are irregular.

questions.question: Jane speaks ___ than before.
questions.correct: An -ly adverb normally forms its comparative with more.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: An -ly adverb normally forms its comparative with more.

questions.question: Tom runs ___ of the three.
questions.correct: Use the adverb superlative for a group of three.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use the adverb superlative for a group of three.

questions.question: She did ___ than yesterday.
questions.correct: better is the irregular comparative of well.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: better is the irregular comparative of well.

narration.text:
比赛时不只比较谁更高，还会比较谁跑得更快。<#0.4#>Amy runs faster than Sue。<#0.8#>faster 说明动作 runs 的速度更高。fast 是短副词，比较级直接加 er，最高级加 est。
若副词以 ly 结尾，通常不把词拉得更长。<#0.4#>Ben answered more carefully than I did。<#0.8#>carefully 前加 more 表示更仔细；三者以上可用 most carefully。Of all the runners, Leo ran the fastest 画出多人范围，用 fastest 选出速度最高者。<#0.7#>
还有不规则形式。Nora performed better than before 中，better 是 well 的比较级；well、better、best 要整体记。badly 则变 worse、worst。
操作时先确认比较的是动作方式或程度，而不是人或物的性质；再看副词形式。短副词常加 er 或 est，多数 ly 副词用 more 或 most；最后检查 well、badly 等不规则变化，并用 than 或范围短语说清比较基准。

examples: The room is warm enough for the baby.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: such modifies the noun phrase a difficult question, and the that-clause gives the result.

exampleNotes.title: Example focus
exampleNotes.body: so directly modifies difficult, and the that-clause gives the result.

rules: enough follows the adjective or adverb it modifies.
too precedes an adjective or adverb and often means “excessively...to...”.
so modifies an adjective or adverb, as in so difficult.
such modifies a noun phrase, as in such a difficult task.

narration.text:
同样是“很暖”，几个程度词站的位置不一样。宝宝待在房间里刚好合适，可以说：<#0.4#>The room is warm enough for the baby。<#0.8#>enough 放在形容词 warm 后，表示程度已经足够。
箱子重到我抬不动，就说：<#0.4#>The box is too heavy for me to lift。<#0.8#>too 放在 heavy 前，表示程度超过合适范围，后面的 for me to lift 说明对谁、做什么来说太重。<#0.7#>
第三句 It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it 中，such 抓住整个名词短语 a difficult question。第四句 The question was so difficult that nobody answered it 里，so 直接修饰形容词 difficult。两句结果相同，程度词后面的结构不同。

even marks an unexpected focus.
almost says an event came close to happening but did not.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: only next to Li Hua focuses on who passed.

narration.text:
一句话只挪动 only，重点就可能换人。<#0.4#>Only Mia solved the puzzle。<#0.8#>only 靠近 Mia，排除的是其他人：只有米娅解开了。第二句 Mia only solved the puzzle 中，only 靠近 solved，更容易表示她只是解开了，没有做别的。副词影响哪一块内容，叫作用范围；位置常在帮我们标范围。<#0.7#>
最后看 Even Ben almost missed the bus。even 把 Ben 标成出乎意料的人，暗示连他都差点误车；almost 修饰 missed，表示事情接近发生，但最后没有真的错过。两个副词在同一句里，各有自己的焦点。<#0.7#>
判断时给 only、even、almost 各画一条括号，圈住它最直接限定的成分；再用排除、意外或接近发生来改述意思。若一句话可能圈出两种范围，就把副词挪到目标成分旁边，或改写句子，让焦点唯一。

exampleNotes.title: Example focus

late means “after the expected time”, while lately means “recently”.

narration.text:
有些副词只差两个字母，意思却拐到另一条路。<#0.4#>He works hard every day。<#0.8#>hard 修饰 works，表示“努力地”。如果换成 hardly，句子就变成“他几乎不工作”，不是“更努力”。
再听：<#0.4#>I have hardly seen her lately。<#0.8#>hardly 表示“几乎没见过”，lately 表示“最近”。这里两个 ly 形式都不能从 hard 和 late 的表面意思直接推出来。<#0.7#>

遇到 hard 或 hardly，先问句子要表达努力，还是几乎不；遇到 late 或 lately，先问是某次到得迟，还是最近这段时间。选完后把中文意思完整代回原句检查，若逻辑突然反转，就说明掉进了同形近形词陷阱。

lessons.title: Ordering multiple adverbials
examples: She sang beautifully on stage last night.
Yesterday, we worked quietly in the library.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: English end position often follows manner–place–time; Chinese commonly gives time and place earlier.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: Time moves first as the setting; manner stays close to the action and place follows.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: carefully before the verb gives manner more focus; end position is also natural but less marked.

rules: A common end order is manner–place–time, though context and focus can change it.
A time or place adverbial can be fronted as a setting and is normally followed by a comma.
A manner adverb can occur before the verb or at the end; the position often changes focus rather than grammaticality.

questions.question: Choose the neutral end order.

narration.text:
一句话同时有“唱得很美、在舞台上、昨晚”，怎样排才不挤？中性说法是：<#0.4#>She sang beautifully on stage last night。<#0.8#>先交代方式 beautifully，再说地点 on stage，最后放时间 last night。这是多个句尾状语常见的“方式、地点、时间”顺序。
顺序不是铁板一块。<#0.4#>Yesterday, we worked quietly in the library。<#0.8#>Yesterday 被提到句首，先搭起昨天这个背景，后面再说怎样工作、在哪里工作。前置的时间或地点状语常与主句用逗号分开。<#0.7#>
She carefully opened the box 把 carefully 放在动词前，让“动作很小心”更早进入听者注意。这个句中位置强调的是方式，而前两句主要展示多个状语在句首和句尾怎样排布。
排列时先把每个状语标成方式、地点或时间；都放句尾时先试方式、地点、时间；若某个信息要承接上文或搭背景，就把它前置并加逗号；最后朗读检查，避免把方式副词硬塞到动词与宾语之间。

narration.text:
同一句 Mia is right，前面换一个副词，说话人的态度就变了。<#0.4#>Perhaps, Mia is right。<#0.8#>perhaps 表示“可能”，不是说明 Mia 怎样做事，而是降低说话人对整件判断的把握。
再看：<#0.4#>Fortunately, nobody was hurt。<#0.8#>nobody was hurt 是事实内容；Fortunately 表示说话人认为这个结果很幸运。这类词不是描写某一个动作，而是在评价整件事。<#0.7#>
Frankly, I disagree 里的 Frankly 也不是说“不同意得很坦率”，而是说明接下来这句话是坦率地讲出来。honestly、briefly 等还能提示说话方式或组织话语。
识别时先把句首副词拿掉，看剩下的主干事实是否完整；再问它表达的是对事实真假的把握、对结果的评价，还是讲话方式。perhaps、probably 属于把握程度，fortunately、sadly 属于评价，frankly、briefly 属于话语态度。别把它们误当成只修饰紧邻的主语。

narration.text:
why、where、how 都能出现在句首，但它们做的事不总一样。直接问离开的原因：<#0.4#>Why did you leave?<#0.8#>Why 是疑问副词，在疑问句中留下“因为什么”的空位，并触发主句疑问语序。
再看地点：<#0.4#>This is the place where we met。<#0.8#>where 不在提问，而是把 we met 接到先行词 place 上，并在从句里表示见面的地点。它既连接名词和定语从句，又在从句内作地点状语，所以叫关系副词。<#0.7#>
Tell me how you solved it 里，how 保留“怎样”的意义，引出一整块“你怎样解决它”的内容，整体作 tell 的宾语。这是疑问副词引导名词性从句，内部要用 you solved 的陈述语序。
判断时先看整句是不是直接提问；是，就按疑问副词处理。若前面有 time、place、reason 等先行词，后面从句在修饰它，就看关系副词；若从句整体回答“告诉、知道、询问什么”，就按名词性从句处理。最后检查它在从句内表示时间、地点、原因还是方式。

narration.text:
hardly 看起来像 hard 加 ly，意思却不是“努力地”。<#0.4#>I hardly know him。<#0.8#>hardly 表示“几乎不”，句子已经接近否定，不能再随手加 not 变成重复否定。
再听：<#0.4#>She rarely complains。<#0.8#>rarely 表示抱怨发生得很少，和 seldom 一样带低频限制。它们不是完全的 no，但已把发生频率压得很低，普通标准英语通常不再和 not 叠用。<#0.7#>
把否定或限制词推到句首，语序还会变化。Never have I seen such a view 先强调“从来没有”，随后把助动词 have 放到主语 I 前，形成部分倒装。这个倒装是句首否定范围带来的正式结构。
操作时先识别 hardly、scarcely、barely、rarely、seldom、never 自带的否定或限制强度；再圈出它们否定的是动作、频率还是范围；若它们位于句首，检查是否需要“助动词加主语加主要动词”的部分倒装。最后删掉没有特殊语境支撑的重复 not。

A conjunctive adverb is not a coordinator; between independent clauses it normally follows a semicolon or period and is followed by a comma.
first, then, meanwhile and finally organize sequence and information flow.

narration.text:
道路封闭，我们换了路线，两件事之间是结果关系。英语可以写：<#0.4#>The road was closed; therefore, we took another route。<#0.8#>therefore 告诉读者后句是前句的结果，但它不是 and、so 那样的并列连词，不能只靠一个逗号把两个完整分句粘起来。这里先用分号结束第一层句界，therefore 后再加逗号。
转折也一样：<#0.4#>The task was difficult; however, we finished it。<#0.8#>however 标出“虽然困难，仍然完成”的反向关系。前面也可以直接用句号，写成两个句子。<#0.7#>
连接副词还能组织顺序。First, check the data; then, write the report 中，First 和 then 帮读者按步骤推进，不是连接两个词或短语。
判断时先看前后是不是各自完整的分句；再辨认副词标的是结果、转折还是顺序。如果用 therefore、however 等连接两个独立分句，前面选分号或句号，后面通常加逗号；不要写成“完整句，however 完整句”的逗号拼接。
